title: Harmonized model intake lane with eval-slicing and pin-expiry safeguards
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Customer requests for new model variants, version pins, and deprecation schedules arrive through multiple channels (support, Sales, Solutions, direct product requests). Engineering and Ops capacity to onboard or pin models is limited. We need a single intake lane that (a) scores requests consistently for enterprise impact and operational cost, (b) enforces staged eval gates and shadow rollouts for safety, and (c) applies timeboxed pin expirations and a default fallback policy to avoid long-term technical debt.

Goal: Define the triage rubric, required eval artifacts, pin-expiry policy, and an operational rollout playbook that Product/Eng/Support can follow with minimal back-and-forth. Deliver a lightweight intake form, automated scoring rules, and a runbook for fast-path (low-risk) vs. stewarded-path (high-risk) requests.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Intake form template published in Confluence and linked from Support/SE playbooks.
A2: Scoring rubric implemented as a spreadsheet and example automation rules (customer-impact, compliance-sensitivity, throughput-cost, stability-risk).
A3: Pin expiry default set to 90 days with automated reminder and re-evaluation workflow; emergency extend process documented.
A4: Eval gate checklist created: synthetic tests, 3 customer prompts, latency/cost benchmark, safety checks. Templates for artifacts (prompts, eval results) must be included.
A5: Rollout playbook for Fast-Lane (<= P2 risk) and Steward-Lane (P0/P1/high-reg) with explicit canary/shadow steps and metrics to abort.
decisions: D1: Use a weighted scoring model combining customer revenue signal (40%), regulatory/data-sensitivity (25%), expected QPS/cost delta (20%), and stability risk (15%).
D2: Default pin duration = 90 days. Shorter pins (30 days) for pilot/sandbox requests; longer pins require SRE + product review and justification.
D3: Eval gate minimum: automated regression on canonical prompt set + perf benchmark within 20% of baseline latency/cost for same sequence distribution.
D4: All P0/P1 requests require a stewarded onboarding with a mandatory shadow canary (traffic mirroring) for at least 72 hours and a post-shadow review.
